text: I took my Forpus parrot to the vet, and the price was exorbitant. The vet was terribly rude, even cursing my bird and saying it could die right then and there. Why would I bring it to the vet if that's the case? We brought it to get better, not to die! I've raised many birds, and I know what happens if a bird is going to die. I don't understand why they would lie. They said admission was the only option and made me sign a document refusing treatment, with a note stating that they had informed me of the risk of death. The price for the first day's admission was 8,500 baht, and then 3,000 baht per day thereafter. Even large animal hospitals in Bangkok don't charge that much, and they have better equipment and facilities. The total cost for medication and treatment that day was 3,300 baht, which is the most expensive I've ever seen. It felt like I was scammed because when I showed the X-ray films to a specialist veterinarian in Bangkok, they said the films were almost unreadable and not clear enough. The vet didn't seem to have enough knowledge of treating exotic animals, yet claimed they could treat my bird. From the first sentence, I knew all birds need deworming medication once a year. Forpus parrots eat grains, so where would they get parasites from? And the price they charged was completely contrary to their knowledge. The vet tried to psychologically manipulate us by saying the animal was going to die, trying to trick us into admitting it, which was really not okay. It felt like we were being deceived and I felt terrible and disappointed. It made it seem like we lacked knowledge. People who keep exotic animals do enough research; they don't just keep them haphazardly. We don't just believe everything the vet says. If anyone is planning to take an exotic animal to this hospital, I would not recommend it. The prices are exorbitant, and the animal might die because the vet is essentially cursing the animal.

text: The staff provided good service, but the treatment itself was lacking. I took my cat to the vet with a cold because she's a stray I adopted. The first visit involved describing the symptoms and then diagnosing it as feline cold. There were no blood tests, no checks for feline AIDS or other diseases; the vet just examined her external symptoms and prescribed medication based on my description. The first visit cost over 2000 baht, and the vet scheduled weekly appointments for a month (1400 baht each week). The vet asked for a second checkup. On that second visit, the vet said the medication had been stopped and she hadn't received any more for another week. I told the vet that my cat wasn't eating well, and the vet diagnosed gingivitis and prescribed more medication (another 2600 baht). Two days later, I contacted the vet again, saying my cat's condition had worsened. She was having diarrhea, eating very little, lethargic, had a fever, and wasn't playing. On March 1st, I went for my next appointment and saw the third vet. The vet said the medication could be stopped because my cat was recovering, having taken all the prescribed medication. The vet reviewed the treatment records and confirmed she had received all the prescribed medication. However, on the last visit, even though she wasn't feverish or having diarrhea but was still lethargic and eating very little, the vet stopped the medication despite her lethargy and poor appetite. After bringing her home late that night, her condition worsened significantly, becoming very severe. On March 2nd, after work, I took her to a new hospital; we changed hospitals altogether. She had a high fever, which cats shouldn't have. She was lethargic and not eating, suggesting a serious illness. It's a dangerous disease that's very worrying. The doctor did blood tests for feline AIDS and thylassemia, but they came back negative. They suspect another disease—I don't remember the name—but her symptoms matched those, and it's a very dangerous and concerning illness. I want to say that Prima Hospital has a lot of doctors, but the treatment from the three female doctors we saw was terrible. They just kept giving her medication endlessly, and never did a single blood test from the first day to the last. The money and time spent on treatment were incredibly wasted; she didn't get better, and her condition even worsened. We saw doctors every week at Prima Hospital and received continuous medication, but nothing worked. We spent tens of thousands of baht, but the treatment was like it was only worth a few hundred. They just treated the symptoms without identifying the root cause. Ultimately, her condition worsened. I forgot to mention, from the first day, no matter how much nasal discharge she had, the doctors just gave her medication to dry it up, but it didn't completely disappear. Even on the last day after stopping the medication, the doctor said the nasal discharge was completely dry, but it didn't go away; some mucus remained in her nose. (This is different from another hospital where they did complete blood tests, checked all blood types, identified potential diseases, and prescribed medication tailored to the specific condition. They also used anesthesia to clear the nasal discharge. With just that, her condition improved noticeably, and it cost less than 1600 baht.) (The doctor scheduled daily anesthesia appointments for my runny nose; he didn't wait for it to get worse, he treated it directly.) The 3 stars I gave are only for the good service and cleanliness of the clinic. As for the treatment itself, I'd only give it one star. Everything in this review is based on my actual experience. Anyone considering treatment there should think carefully; I wouldn't recommend it.

They updated me on his eating and sleeping habits, took him to the grassy area behind the hospital to play, and provided constant updates. They're open 24 hours a day. They can treat any condition, and it's the safest place to go. When they took him to the hospital at midnight, his condition was very bad. In the morning, when his mother visited him, he was cheerful, eating on his own, and drinking normally. The doctors were truly excellent.
